works.note: Kemble's verse translation sets roughly one line per OE half-line (1055 lines for 550), so it is mapped in blocks. Section i of the translation = section i of the OE (same titles, same breaks). The 44 speaker labels ('Saturnus cwæð:' / 'Saturn spake.', 'Salomon quoth.') match one for one and every speech begins a chunk; longer speeches are cut further at sentence starts where an OE line and a Kemble line begin together. oe_lines count the OE text's non-empty lines from each section's first number, speaker labels included, as the app does; tr_lines are 1-based non-empty-line indices within the matching translation section. Kemble's asterisks for gaps in the manuscript stay inside the chunk they fall in.

line_numbering.poems: All 'oe' and 'tr' numbers in poems[].translations[].exceptions are 1-based indices of NON-EMPTY lines of each poem's text field (blank lines skipped). For the OE texts this equals ASPR numbering except where a poem has heading lines (Waldhere 'I'/'II'), prose rubrics (charms) or 'Finit.'. For prose translations each paragraph is one non-empty line, so 'tr' numbers are paragraph numbers.
line_numbering.exceptions_format: ['1:1'] = translation line n faces OE line n throughout. Otherwise a full piecewise map: {'oe':[a,b],'tr':[c,d]} segments in order; 'oe': null = translation lines with no OE (headings, conjectural supplements, footnotes); 'tr': null = OE lines left untranslated (charm rubrics, omitted lines); 'per_line': 2 = each OE line takes two translation lines (Thorpe sets every half-line on its own line). In 'blocks' mode the same segments define the blocks to top-align side by side.
line_numbering.works: oe_lines are ASPR line numbers, as in the OE sections' 'Lines a-b' titles (Genesis: continuous A+B numbering; Meters of Boethius: each meter numbered from 1, matched by oe_section). Kennedy chunks use tr_paras = 1-based non-empty-line indices in the single translation section.

notes.riddle_numbering: Faust & Thompson and Spaeth titles use the Krapp-Dobbie/Tupper numbers (I-LX = ASPR 1-60). Brougham's 'LXXIX. A Falcon' is ASPR 80 (Grein-Wülker numbering). Gordon's numbers are not reliable as ASPR numbers: 'LIX. A Chalice' is ASPR 48 (not 59), 'LXXX' = ASPR 81, 'LXXXIV' = 85, 'LXXXV' = 86; all Gordon riddles were matched by content. ASPR 59 (the other chalice riddle) has no Gordon translation; Thorpe's 1st-series LX translates it. Thorpe 1842 numbers the Exeter riddles in three series (I-LX, then I, then I-XXX) that do not match ASPR; all 38 Thorpe riddles were matched by content (e.g. 1st series V = ASPR 4, XXXI = 30, LX = 59; 2nd series I = 30b; 3rd series I = 61, XXV + XXVI = 88, XXX = 95).
special_pairings: Gordon's 'The Soul's Address to the Body' is a composite: Part II (saved soul) exists only in Vercelli (Soul and Body I), but Part I also uses Exeter-only readings (Soul and Body II 94, 101, 107). It is paired with both, paragraph-mapped to each.
Gordon's 'Riddle XXXV. A Coat of Mail' (Exeter Riddle 35) is also paired, at medium confidence, with The Leiden Riddle (its Northumbrian version).
Faust & Thompson's Cædmon's Hymn (made from the West Saxon text) and Bede's Death Song (follows the Northumbrian reading) are paired with every OE version on the site.
Faust & Thompson's Maxims I gives only ASPR 71-106; Charm 1 and Charm 4 give only the verse incantations; Cook & Tinker's Nine Herbs Charm is verse to line 44 and prose after.
Thorpe's 3rd-series Riddles XXV and XXVI are one riddle in ASPR (88); the site's translation joins them.
The Rune Poem (Dickins), the Menologium (Fox), and Sweet's Pastoral Care preface and epilogue are paired as blocks: per stanza, per sentence, and whole poem.

notes.method: Every pair was checked by printing OE and translation side by side (full text for short poems, every 4th-10th line plus the ends for long ones, full view wherever counts differed), so the segment maps are line-exact for the 'lines' pairs except where marked 'approximate'. Long-work boundaries were found by reading the OE first lines of each section against the translation text. The 52 pairs of 15 Oct 2026 (Thorpe's riddles and longer Exeter poems, Kemble, Ingram, Fox, Dickins, Sweet) were checked by printing every OE line against its two half-line translation lines in full; every drift point was read and given its own segment.
